title: Read a name in the path
summary: Laravel: Read a name in the path. Visit /hello/Asha.
introduction: Curly braces mark a route input. Open GET /hello/Ravi. Read the example, then check the result.
learningObjectives: Read a name in the path with Laravel

blocks.text: Create a practice Laravel project with Composer, then replace routes/web.php with one example. Start php artisan serve --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8000. These read-only starter routes need no database.
Read a name in the path

blocks.title: Read a name in the path
blocks.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => response("Hi, " . $name . "!")->header("Content-Type", "text/plain"));

blocks.text: The route captures Ravi as name. The response declares plain text so it displays the greeting literally.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Do not place raw user input in HTML.
